rules: Tracked Rust source only; source files are counted once, including build.rs and feature variants.
Every nonblank production line counts, including comments, inline tests and owned generated semantic code. Dedicated tests/examples/fixtures are reported separately.
src/native_tests.rs is only compiled under cfg(test); counter-extension is a dev-dependency test fixture.
Existing/planned owner paths identify responsibilities, not a promise to copy each Rust module or a claim that absent Nupp files exist.
All source variants are counted. All-features metadata is a dependency union, not a buildable runtime configuration: allocator features are mutually exclusive.

No tracked Rust file is classified as unchanged third-party or mechanically generated binding. Generated link sidecars are reported separately as local artifacts; they are not a semantic source exemption.

execution.action: Replace Rust dispatch and instruction semantics with Nupp handlers; later-phase state services remain named and cannot execute guest instructions.

objects.action: Integrate the existing Nupp heap/collector; move representation, accounting and rooted storage semantics there.

tasks.action: Move scheduler, frame lifecycle, cleanup, coroutine and supervision policy into Nupp.

workers.action: Move heap/transfer/channel, admission and completion policy into Nupp. Its reactor and worker model own blocking work; only thread creation stays in the bridge.

host.action: Move the reactor, parking/completion and resource policy into Nupp with direct C system calls. Delete Rust host-I/O orchestration; retain only allowed page/thread/platform primitives in the small bridge.

graph.action: Use the single-IR Nupp graph and move semantic/proof verification into Nupp; no Rust CFG reconstruction.

images.action: Move loading, verification, linking/code identities and replacement publication into Nupp.

snapshots.action: Move value graph saves, checkpoints, resource transactions, history and replay into Nupp; retain all feature gates.

library.action: Move builtin/library dispatch, validation and lifetimes into Nupp. Host I/O uses the Nupp reactor and direct C calls; essential compression/cryptographic library implementations may remain behind thin calls.

patterns.action: Adopt the Nupp Pattern plan and delete nregex plus the regex dependency; add no Rust regex/PEG engine.

foreign.action: Nupp owns FFI layout checks, resource lifetime and callback policy; the bridge only enters libraries and supplies trampolines.

tiers.action: Delete guest semantic emitters/specializers after handler-derived tiers consume the Nupp graph; keep only machine-code generation interfaces.

simd.action: Move interpretation/reference semantics into Nupp handlers and derive compiled SIMD from the shared graph.

pages.action: Retain narrow executable-memory mapping/protection calls; move tiering/admission policy into Nupp.

entry.action: Consolidate startup/embedding and native links into one bridge crate; policy and VM behavior live in Nupp.

abi.action: Consolidate C ABI/layout declarations and narrow error crossings into the bridge; no opaque VM semantics.

checksum.action: Retain narrow third-party digest/checksum entry points; Nupp owns validation, lifetimes and policies.

compression.action: Consolidate library calls into the bridge; Nupp owns streaming/resource/error policy.

files.action: Delete the Rust files provider, queues and blocking lanes. Nupp owns file I/O, globbing, cancellation and resource policy through direct C calls and its own blocking-work pool.

gpu.action: Keep the common Nupp graph and GPU ownership model; optional second GPU bridge only if its dependency boundary warrants it.

http.action: Delete Reqwest and the Rust HTTP provider. Implement HTTP/1.1 client and server, parser, pooling, deadlines and policy in Nupp over its reactor; fuzz the parser from its first commit.

net.action: Delete the Rust net provider. Nupp owns socket operations through direct C calls, readiness/completion backends, queues and resource policy; network resources are not restored.

platform.action: Consolidate page/time/UUID/thread/platform primitives into the bridge; Nupp owns resources and policy.

process.action: Delete the Rust process provider. Nupp owns spawn, pipes, exit, kill, cancellation and lifetimes through direct system calls and its reactor.

executor.action: Delete Tokio and the Rust shared async executor/readiness implementation. Nupp owns the reactor, scheduler, deadlines and blocking-work pool; only thread creation stays in the bridge.

tls.action: Delete the Rust TLS provider and Tokio adapter. Use one I/O-free TLS library through a C call; Nupp owns sockets, ciphertext flow, trust-store integration, cancellation and resource policy. No TLS or cryptography implementation is written in Nupp.

test.action: Retain or port the executable fixture when its implementation is replaced; not a product crate/source exemption for inline tests.

dependencies.scope: Unfiltered workspace all-feature package-resolution union, including dev/build and platform-specific dependencies; not a default executable dependency count.

generatedArtifacts.classification: Generated handler link declarations, ABI/dispatch tables and assertions; audit generated behavior independently, do not hide owned semantics here.

ownershipPlanUpdate.decision: Nupp owns the reactor, blocking pool, file/process/network layers and HTTP/1.1 through direct C calls. Delete Tokio, Reqwest and Rust host-I/O providers; TLS is one I/O-free library. Networking is not restored.
